findings.where: the four checklist cards; pwa.json in full (356 bytes)
findings.what: The iPhone-facing artifact says nothing about the substitute. The four cards are network and install only ('this one, the iphone' / 'put this phone on the tailnet' / 'install the profile the other phone is serving' / 'add it to the home screen'), and pwa.json records manifest name, display, start_url, 4 icons, apple_touch_icon and one service worker - nothing about what replaces the motor. findings.where: `asked_a_motor_for` in every report; the 09_two_devices.png and 16_setup_android.png entries in WHY_MISSING.json
findings.what: No artifact in the set contains a vibration. Every motor ask is answered 'no motor in a browser: the page rhythm carries it instead', and 09_two_devices.png / 16_setup_android.png are absent because /dev/kvm is missing (adbd answered after 113 minutes with no framework behind it). The row's central test - identifiable by haptic pattern alone with the screen face down - is therefore argued from a derived measure in logs/haptics.check.json rather than shown on a device.
findings.why: The reason is a reason and not an excuse, and the derived measure is sound (I reproduced it), but it is still the largest thing about this row that the set cannot show, and it is why the two-device frame the row is named against does not exist.

what_is_working: The substitute channel is a faithful, frame-accurate rendering of each pattern's envelope, not a decoration. Measuring page translation by FFT phase correlation of the page furniture (window y 200-776, x 80-976, full resolution) against the first frame of each run of 07_feeling_landing.mp4: `hold` (900@142 off100 900@142) steps to -12 px for frames 1-56 (896 ms), returns to -1..-2 for frames 57-62 (~96 ms), steps back to -12 for frames 63-118 (896 ms) and releases by f135; `squeeze` (80@78 / 160@138 / 320@198) gives three plateaus of -5, -11 and -17 px rising with amplitude; `nuzzle` (90@134 x3 then 400@98) gives three short -8/-9 dips then a longer shallower -6/-7 press of ~25 frames (400 ms); `soup` (150@119, 150@119, 600@156) gives two short dips then a 37-frame (592 ms) deeper plateau. The same `hold` signature recurs in 08_state_propagating.mp4 frames 16-164 (two 56-frame plateaus, a 6-frame return between, total excursion 13 px).

The user-authored feeling drives that channel identically to a built-in, sent by a local gesture. In 15_authored_feeling.mp4, `letGo` at f145 fires `pigeon` (30@175 off80 x3, off300, 200@140; logs/15_authored_feeling.report.json records the motor ask at amp 175). Measured against the settled page at f219: three sharp -17/-16/-15 px spikes at frames 146-148, 153-155 and 160-162, spaced 7 frames (112 ms) apart, a gap over frames 169-179, then a sustained -11..-15 px from f180 to f193 (224 ms) settling to 0 by f202 - three taps and a longer press, exactly the published string.

Identifiability survives an independent reimplementation. I rebuilt the felt-distance measure from the `segments` in logs/haptics.json (40 ms bins, amplitude^0.6, mean absolute difference x100, best alignment over a +/-15% tempo search, plus a length term with a 15% deadband) over all 630 pairs: smallest 17.78 on empty_chair/come_home - the same closest pair, and within 0.04 of the 17.74 the file reports. Deriving the floor the same way (half-Weber twins max 3.21, double-Weber twins min 13.36, geometric midpoint 6.55) puts the closest real pair 2.7x above it; against the file's own 8.7 it is 2.0x above. The bands do not overlap and no pair is under either floor.

The vocabulary is there and it is in the pictures: 34 built-in feelings in 6 named families (Warmth 6, Ache 5, Shelter 7, Mischief 7, Static 6, Sparkle 5), all 36 laid on one 2700 ms scale in crops/haptics_strip.png, 36 distinct haptic strings, and a distinct object id and sound id for every one. All six family tabs are shown open in 15_authored_feeling.mp4 - WARMTH f14, SHELTER f32, SPARKLE f51, MISCHIEF f70, ACHE f84, STATIC f98.

A feeling arrives as a thing, and a state does not. 01_pulse.png y 1150-1560 is a shelf of six different objects - a chair drawn in ink on torn paper, a scrawl, scattered confetti, a pale rounded form, a pink wrapped sweet, a folded card - each with its name and time; crops/04_moments_what_we_felt.png is a whole 'what we felt' timeline of the same objects sorted by who sent them. In 08_state_propagating.mp4 the partner's states arrive as thin grey annotation rows ('noor - out', 'noor is heads down', 'noor is quiet') while the feeling arrives as the soup object, so the two kinds are visibly different kinds.

Twelve partner-state signals are on the glass in 01_pulse.png - MOOD, HERE, WHERE, NEED, ENERGY, BATTERY, LAST UP, THEIR CLOCK, RINGER, MOVING, SIGNAL, AT HOME - plus the standing line above them; logs/01_pulse.report.json `partner_signals` carries 14 keys.

One-gesture reach is present in every region. In a 120x120 box at x 1320-1440, y 2830-2950 of each 1440x3120 still, the bottom 20 rows are 0.52-0.61 pale in all five region stills (01_pulse, 02_chat, 03_us, 04_moments, 05_settings) - the same corner fold - and 15_authored_feeling.mp4 shows it opening the picker in two of them (US f0-100, Pulse f220-235).

Sideways never goes further than up, and the board really turns. |dx| < |dy| in all four runs of 07 (8.3 vs 13.9, 9.0 vs 17.1, 2.1 vs 10.0, 6.6 vs 13.2). Phase-correlating a left band and a right band of the card separately over the `hold` run, dy(right) - dy(left) across 560 px runs -0.6 to -1.0 px through each plateau and returns to ~0 in the 100 ms gap: 0.0011-0.0018 rad, consistent with haptics.json's -0.00375 rad at full amplitude scaled by 142/255.

The voice holds. logs/strings.json reads 563 strings and finds nothing; re-checking all 1,145 strings in the file myself, the only '!' hits are Dart null-assertion operators (`${tearId!}_edge`), the single 'user' is inside the checker's own rule text, and no marketing phrase or app name appears outside the rule patterns.

Audio is real and per-feeling: 07_feeling_landing.mp4 carries a mono AAC track whose RMS in 40 ms windows rises from silence at exactly frames 0, 150, 221 and 314 - the four arrival frames logs/07_feeling_landing.sound.json names - with four different peak levels. The log says plainly that the file is the feeling's own ogg mixed in rather than a recording of the app.
The second lighting condition holds up: crops/dusk_pulse.png shows the same shelf of feelings under a warm low key with long cast shadows, and logs/dusk_pulse.report.json confirms `light: "dusk"`.
verdict: Judged on what the pictures actually do, the transmission is real and I could measure it: in 07_feeling_landing.mp4 and 08_state_propagating.mp4 the page moves to each feeling's published envelope to within a frame - hold's two 896 ms plateaus with a 96 ms release between them, squeeze's three plateaus of -5, -11 and -17 px rising with amplitude, nuzzle's three taps and a longer press - and in 15_authored_feeling.mp4 a user-authored feeling sent by a local gesture drives that same channel to its own string. Rebuilding the separability measure from scratch reproduces the file's closest pair to within 0.04 and puts it 2.7x above a floor I derived myself, 34 built-ins sit in six named families all shown open, twelve partner signals are on the glass, the corner is in all five regions, and a feeling arrives as an object with a shadow and its own sound while a state arrives as a grey annotation - which is exactly the distinction the row is asking for. What holds it below the floor is that the evidence for the half of the row about state propagating does not stand up: 08_state_propagating.mp4 fails the brief's own held-frame test on 92 of 735 frames, and the freeze is precisely the reconnect this cycle added - 47 frames of the note stuck at 'going', a cut, then 45 frames of it reading 'sent', with the far phone's second note never appearing at all - so the one thing the clip was reshot to show is delivered as two stills. Around that sit four more real defects: the one press-and-hold in the whole set shows nothing for 640 ms because the script holds over a tile that is not on the sheet; both authored feelings are the seventh tile of their family and are cut off unnamed by the picker's bottom edge at y=1950; logs/surfaces.json skips both authored objects and then reports zero holes; and the pocket read-back added this cycle came back with held_by_the_phone still empty, on a phone that was still on its setup checklist. None of these is the concept failing - the concept is working, and better than its own record admits - but two of the three artifacts this row is named against cannot carry it, and the third does not exist.
